developer.title: Developer feedback
developer.purpose: Cheap source and stable-reference checks suitable for routine edits.

pr.title: Pull-request evidence
pr.purpose: Durable implementation, conformance, policy, and static-quality checks used at the public integration boundary.

research-checkpoint.title: Research checkpoint
research-checkpoint.purpose: Bounded semantic witnesses and falsifiers used when closing a coherent redesign boundary.

scheduled.title: Scheduled deep checks
scheduled.purpose: Broader research reruns and diagnostics whose latency is unsuitable for edit-time feedback.

release-freeze.title: Release or specification freeze
release-freeze.purpose: All locally executable durable and bounded research checks, including the canonical expensive Analysis run.

formal-reading.title: Pinned formal reading
formal-reading.purpose: Externally provisioned reading of formalization receipts against the pinned upstream checkout.

checks.title: Check-control self-tests
checks.subject: The manifest parser, selector, command resolver, and structured result writer.
checks.claim: The checked control-plane invariants hold for the committed manifest and synthetic runner cases.
nonclaims: This does not validate the semantics or implementation exercised by any child check.

checks.title: Validation method portfolio
checks.subject: The diversity of evidence methods declared for each check classification.
checks.claim: Every inventoried check meets the low structural method floor for its classification, and the complete method inventory is emitted.
nonclaims: Meeting a structural method floor does not grade test quality, independence, completeness, or the truth of any exercised claim.

checks.title: Evaluation lifecycle inventory
checks.subject: The ownership, disposition, and tracked footprint of every evaluation package.
checks.claim: Every research check and tracked evaluation package has exactly one declared lifecycle disposition, and the measured inventory is emitted.
nonclaims: Lifecycle coverage and size measurements do not grade research quality, promote a package, or authorize automatic deletion.

checks.title: Open items index
checks.subject: The complete set of publicly recorded open items: `CannotAnswer` findings in frozen research findings, reopening records under the design notes, and the rows of the public gap ledger.
checks.claim: Every frozen findings file parses under strict JSON, every `CannotAnswer` finding carries a well-formed code (a code shared by two findings of one package is reported, not failed), every reopening record states its state, and the regenerated index is emitted.
nonclaims: An index of open items grades nothing and closes nothing; an item leaves it only when its owning ledger changes, and private ledgers are outside its scope.

checks.title: Public-tree boundary
checks.subject: Repository paths forbidden from the public source tree.
checks.claim: No tracked path violates the public-tree policy encoded by the guard.
nonclaims: A passing guard does not classify untracked files or establish document authority.

checks.title: Python semantic-reference self-check
checks.subject: The durable Python semantic twin and its embedded known-answer and negative cases.
checks.claim: The reference package accepts and rejects its committed bounded corpus as declared.
nonclaims: Self-consistency is not independence from the specification or the C++ implementation.

checks.title: Python reference canonical laws
checks.subject: Canonical values, loading, identity digests, and the compatibility facade of the durable twin.
checks.claim: The bounded canonical corpus matches an independent encoder, round trips, preserves declared metamorphic laws, and refuses its negative mutations.
nonclaims: Finite canonical-law agreement is not collision resistance, an exhaustive test of the unbounded value domain, or compiler correctness.

checks.title: Python reference architecture
checks.subject: The durable twin's lower-layer dependency directions and isolation from project implementations.
checks.claim: The checked module dependency boundaries hold over every current top-level reference module.
nonclaims: A clean dependency graph does not establish semantic completeness, independence of every algorithm, or compiler correctness.

checks.title: Python defect lint
checks.subject: Tracked Python sources under the repository-wide Ruff policy.
checks.claim: The selected static defect rules report no finding.
nonclaims: Lint success is not functional, semantic, security, or style completeness.

checks.title: Rust emitter unit suites
checks.subject: The Rust emitter workspace package.
checks.claim: The emitter unit and integration cases pass under the locked dependency graph.
nonclaims: The selected Rust cases do not establish backend correctness for all inputs.

checks.title: Rust runtime integration suites
checks.subject: The runtime package under its toy and pinned-upstream feature surfaces.
checks.claim: The selected runtime cases pass under the locked dependency graph.
nonclaims: The selected feature cases do not establish general runtime or upstream conformance.

checks.title: Rust static analysis
checks.subject: All Rust workspace targets and features under Clippy.
checks.claim: Clippy reports no warning under the configured locked workspace.
nonclaims: Static-analysis success is not functional or semantic correctness.

checks.title: Rust formatting
checks.subject: Rust workspace source formatting.
checks.claim: Rustfmt would make no change to the workspace sources.
nonclaims: Formatting success carries no behavioral claim.

checks.title: C++ and MLIR compiler suite
checks.subject: The configured native build's lit suite and four pure-core unit executables.
checks.claim: The configured build passes the committed compiler, tool, differential, and unit corpus.
nonclaims: Corpus success is not compiler correctness, protocol security, or production readiness.

checks.title: Pinned formalization-receipt reading
checks.subject: Declared formalization receipts read against the pinned ArkLib checkout.
checks.claim: The external workflow can classify the receipts against the exact pinned source revision.
nonclaims: A successful reading is not a compiler-build result, runtime input, or proof of every project claim.

checks.title: Cross-owner semantic closure
checks.subject: The bounded cross-owner semantic closure research model.
checks.claim: The committed finite closure cases satisfy their declared structural and identity laws.
nonclaims: This finite research model is not a product implementation or a semantic completeness proof.

checks.title: Semantic-profile publication
checks.subject: The indexed target-profile publication model and independent compiler.
checks.claim: Both finite publication paths agree on the committed profiles and reject the selected mutations.
nonclaims: Publication agreement is not target evaluator, theorem, or runtime conformance evidence.

checks.title: Recursive-composition boundary
checks.subject: The finite owner-boundary model for recursive composition.
checks.claim: The selected composition shapes preserve the declared ownership and handoff constraints.
nonclaims: This is not a recursion implementation or an IVC, PCD, or preservation theorem.

checks.title: Structural protocol expressibility axes
checks.subject: A closed structural-feature matrix that routes each value to one current constructor or profile, listed Core reopening condition, or explicit boundary without using protocol-family names as derivation rules.
checks.claim: All 63 frozen case vectors are total over 20 closed axes, derive their frozen fits, bends, or breaks verdict and exact obstruction set, and reproduce eight holdout-adjudication records and 22 split peer-review records with no disagreement.
nonclaims: This closed authored matrix is not a universal protocol taxonomy, machine-checked source correspondence, Core or profile implementation result, compiler-support claim, theorem, cryptographic property, or deployment evidence.

checks.title: Interactive protocol and Fiat-Shamir contracts
checks.subject: The bounded InteractiveCore, transcript-binding, and Fiat-Shamir contract model.

checks.title: Pre-freeze Fiat-Shamir assurance pressure
checks.subject: The finite ten-layer Fiat-Shamir assurance model, separating exact logical challenge prefixes, closed external-Statement correspondence, typed encoding, concrete state-transition binding, challenge-sampler adequacy, oracle-process correspondence, interactive source properties and theorem application, static OIR projection, realization and parser conformance, and deployment composition, together with its sixteen-case attack matrix.
checks.claim: The finite positive controls and attack-shaped mutations produce their expected qualified outcomes in every layer: exact-prefix and closed-Statement checks detect omitted, reordered, duplicated, and substituted material; the typed length-delimited, complete-limb, and full-width encoders have no alias in the enumerated domains while the unframed, trailing-zero, and high-bit-truncated encoders expose explicit aliases; total exact-uniform and conditional-with-failure sampler contracts stay distinct over the complete enumerated draw spaces; the exact static projection and bounded realization vectors detect a dropped prefix law, a weak query index, and unconsumed proof bytes; and a security request stays incomplete when theorem, source-property, or QROM premises are absent, with the all-green chain retaining evidence kind bounded-control.
nonclaims: It does not prove injectivity outside the selected finite domains, collision resistance, sponge security, random-oracle correspondence, state-restoration or round-by-round soundness, theorem truth, OIR correctness, compiler correctness, implementation conformance, parser safety, QROM security, or deployment readiness.

The finite limb and truncation cases are advisory-shaped witnesses: they demonstrate the class of semantic distinction exposed by CVE-2026-46654 but do not reproduce Plonky3's field, permutation, exploit, or patched code.
